title: [bug] [alpha.17] [windows] Cannot instantiate more than one window on some machines
body:
### Describe the bug

When I try to instantiate more than one window - either using `WindowBuilder` or by having more than one entry in the `windows` config array - on some Windows machine the app consistently dies and shows `failed to create webview: WebView2 error: WindowsError(Error { code: HRESULT(0x8007139F), message: "The group or resource is not in the correct state to perform the requested operation." })` on the console.

This is only reproducible on some Windows machines (I managed to reproduce it on 1 out of 3 I tried), but on that one it is produced very consistently. I suspect it's linked to OneDrive (the machine where it fails is using OneDrive).

The workaround was to remove all the entries from the `windows` config array, and instantiate all the windows manually while setting different `data_directory` built from `app_data_dir` with different subdirectories attached to it. I suspect it might be a good idea to instantiate all windows with their own data_directory by default, at least on Windows.

### Reproduction

 * Run npm create tauri-app@latest --alpha
 * Add a second entry to the `windows` array in the config
 * Run the app

### Expected behavior

Two windows open

### Platform and versions

```text
[✔] Environment
    - OS: Windows 10.0.20348 X64
    ✔ WebView2: 118.0.2088.76
    ✔ MSVC: Visual Studio Community 2022
    ✔ rustc: 1.72.0 (5680fa18f 2023-08-23)
    ✔ cargo: 1.72.0 (103a7ff2e 2023-08-15)
    ✔ rustup: 1.26.0 (5af9b9484 2023-04-05)
    ✔ Rust toolchain: stable-x86_64-pc-windows-msvc (default)
    - node: 18.13.0
    - yarn: 1.22.19
    - npm: 8.19.3

[-] Packages
    - tauri [RUST]: 2.0.0-alpha.17
    - tauri-build [RUST]: 2.0.0-alpha.11
    - wry [RUST]: 0.34.2
    - tao [RUST]: 0.23.0
    - @tauri-apps/api [NPM]: 2.0.0-alpha.11
    - @tauri-apps/cli [NPM]: 2.0.0-alpha.17

[-] App
    - build-type: bundle
    - CSP: unset
    - distDir: ../dist
    - devPath: http://localhost:1420/
    - bundler: Vite
```


### Stack trace

```text
failed to create webview: WebView2 error: WindowsError(Error { code: HRESULT(0x8007139F), message: "The group or resource is not in the correct state to perform the requested operation." })
```


### Additional context

_No response_

comments.author: participant3
comments.body: @participant4 Any thoughts on timing? We switched from 1.x to 2.x for some useful Mac improvements, but are now blocked on Windows 11 on 3 different machines. It's alpha so at our own risk; that's fine. Just trying to decide whether we can afford to wait or have to go back to 1.x.

comments.author: participant4
comments.body:
No idea. There are 2 bugs here though. one in webview2 itself (fixed in their canary builds) which makes it crash basically always, and something in tauri that crashes it _sometimes_ (this is what this issue was about).

I hope microsoft pushes that fix to stable asap. We're close to their regular release date though so hopefully it'll be part of that.

For the tauri specific issue i'm not sure how to best handle the race condition yet (using seperate data dirs as proposed in OP's message is not a good solution imo, since those folders are already larger than we'd like), we're looking into it though.

comments.author: participant4
comments.body:
Alrighty, so i spent the whole day on this and did not get much further.

All i know is that the crash happens here https://github.com/tauri-apps/wry/blob/dev/src/webview2/mod.rs#L304-L316. I tried to get more info with debuggers but just couldn't get more than the error we already had...

Also i think the issue is that _something_ goes wrong with the first webview data dir registration which makes all subsequent ones fail because i tried to add some auto retry mechanism by either just retrying the linked call or including a new webview2 environment object as suggested in their docs. Both did not work, they just kept on failing with the same error.

If nobody in the team (or the community) has any more ideas i will open an issue in the webview2 repo over the weekend because i consider this a blocker for v2.

p.s. to reproduce this, just use the multiwebview example in wry, you may have to set the same user data dir for all 4 webviews but letting the webview use the default path also causes this error, just a bit less frequent i think. You can also reproduce this with the multiwindow example if you spam the button **really** fast, or easier by changing the code to spawn 2-4 windows in quick succession.

p.p.s. Until the next webview2 runtime release, don't forget to use the canary runtime to test this.

comments.author: participant2
comments.body:
Good news!
I think Microsoft finally fixed the critical bug they had and released it into stable version!

To update it:
1. Open microsoft edge (stable, the regular) from search
2. Open `edge://settings/help` and check that version is ` 120.0.2210.144` or greater or wait for it to update
3. Rerun your app and ensure that it uses version ` 120.0.2210.144` or later using `tauri::webview_version()`

comments.author: participant8
comments.body:
The argument passed to ICoreWebView2EnvironmentOptions.SetAdditionalBrowserArguments seems to be inconsistent in [wry](https://github.com/tauri-apps/wry/blob/f8761fbaaa38ef434740e371041ea099fcaf6037/src/webview2/mod.rs#L201).
Default argument string is "--disable-features=msWebOOUI,msPdfOOUI,msSmartScreenProtection --autoplay-policy=no-user-gesture-required" and its code points should be

` [45, 45, 100, 105, 115, 97, 98, 108, 101, 45, 102, 101, 97, 116, 117, 114, 101, 115, 61, 109, 115, 87, 101, 98, 79, 79, 85, 73, 44, 109, 115, 80, 100, 102, 79, 79, 85, 73, 44, 109, 115, 83, 109, 97, 114, 116, 83, 99, 114, 101, 101, 110, 80, 114, 111, 116, 101, 99, 116, 105, 111, 110, 32, 45, 45, 97, 117, 116, 111, 112, 108, 97, 121, 45, 112, 111, 108, 105, 99, 121, 61, 110, 111, 45, 117, 115, 101, 114, 45, 103, 101, 115, 116, 117, 114, 101, 45, 114, 101, 113, 117, 105, 114, 101, 100]`

But code points sometimes become different like [16560, 21260, 607], [26016, 48040, 354].

Error occurs when first WebView is created with invalid argument and the second WebView is created with valid argument.
Webviews are created successfully when both arguments are valid or invalid(ignorable).

I don't even know if this inconsistency is expected and irrelevant to the error, but this was the only difference I observed.
